coverage_status_note: Sites mapped to grids. No documents read, so no claim to check.
claims_absent_note: We have ingested no sustainability report or filing from this operator, so there is nothing of its own to hold against the grid. This is a gap in our coverage, not a finding about them.

sites.note: confidence=high. The 10-K power-provider table names Denton Municipal Electric at 297 MW. Core Scientific OWNS this campus; CoreWeave is its tenant (separate row). Converting from bitcoin mining to AI/HPC colocation.
confidence=high. The 10-K lists the Cottonwood site at 253 MW served by Texas-New Mexico Power; Reeves County is the ERCOT Far West weather zone, the same Permian footprint the detector ranks 2nd.

confidence=low. The 10-K lists Dalton 1-3 at 195 MW served by Dalton Utilities, so the utility is stated by an SEC filing. The SOCO balancing-authority attribution for this north Georgia municipal utility was NOT confirmed and is the weak link in this row.
confidence=high. The 10-K names TVA as power provider for the 150 MW Marshall County site. Far western Kentucky is TVA, not LG&E/KU - a state-level mapping would get this wrong.

confidence=high. The 10-K electric-utility-provider table names Oklahoma Gas & Electric at 100 MW for Muskogee OK. OG&E is its own SPP sub-region, so this resolves cleanly rather than sitting at bare SWPP.

confidence=high. The 10-K table names Murphy Electric Power Board at 35 MW for Marble NC. Murphy EPB is a municipal TVA distributor in Cherokee County, so this site is TVA. Deliberately split from Marble 2 next door, which the same table puts on Duke - two adjacent facilities in one town on two DIFFERENT balancing authorities, which is exactly the kind of split a geographic mapping destroys.

confidence=medium. The 10-K table names Duke Energy at 68 MW for Marble NC, adjacent to Marble 1 on Murphy EPB/TVA. Far western NC is Duke Energy Carolinas rather than Duke Energy Progress, so DUK not CPLE; that sub-split is inferred from service territory, the utility itself is stated.

confidence=low. The 10-K table names Nodak Electric Cooperative at 100 MW for Grand Forks ND, so the utility is stated by an SEC filing. The BA is the weak link: Nodak is a Minnkota Power Cooperative member and eastern North Dakota is generally MISO, but MISO vs SWPP/WAUE for ND cooperative load was NOT confirmed. Same uncertainty as the Applied Digital Harwood row.

talk_score_method: magnitude x specificity x scope_breadth, 0-1. How big the number is, how precisely it is stated, and how little it is hedged. Narrowing qualifiers (annual, market-based, certificates, owned-and-operated) reduce scope_breadth.
walk_score_method: mean physical carbon-free share across mapped sites, calendar 2025, all hours, grid-only, unweighted by site size.
notes: Grid-only. Excludes power purchase agreements and renewable energy certificates.
Unweighted across sites; we do not know each site's load.
Site mapping is hand-curated from serving utilities, never inferred from state.
Annual matched claims are TRUE under the GHG Protocol market-based method. The verdict is 'true on paper, X physically', not an accusation.
